首先游戏还不错，但是存在几点问题，配上68的价格就差强人意了 1.暂停时使用键盘移动视角，视角移动速度非常慢，必须使用鼠标拖拽视角 2.黄昏时，螃蟹会前往堡垒附近防守夜晚的敌人，建筑师站在堡垒间隔一个位置，猎手站在间隔三个位置，如果选择了减少攻击范围的祝福，猎手会一直发呆直到堡垒被敌人打爆，此时你如果手动触发攻击指令，建筑师会向前攻击敌人，猎手还是一动不动 3.敌人太多时模型重叠，无法选中堡垒修复 4.螃蟹喂食动画太慢，后期食物螃蟹多了按了加速还是要喂半天 5.有一类螃蟹升级天赋是，在水草、珊瑚附近时每秒增加x的xp，但是螃蟹的经验值是通过食物增加的一个食物应该是1点，没有看出这一类的螃蟹升级可以使螃蟹的经验值获得提升，不确定是翻译问题还是我没有理解 6.需要增加多倍速功能。一般的这类游戏都有。 7.内容还是太少，亟待增加

[h2]前言[/h2] 本作是Chaos Theory Games开发的一款带有轻微rogue属性的策略游戏，你讲扮演螃蟹之神带领子嗣们度过一次又一次的迁徒，一路向前海洋深处钳行。 [h2]玩法[/h2] 开局选定五位蟹蟹宝宝其中之一成为螃蟹之神（并无属性加成），然后带领四位螃蟹宝宝迁徒，每张地图的目标都是收集足够的食物就可以通关，难度高的时候往往需要收集比关卡所需更多的食物（上限是两倍）来应对之后波次。选择对应职业构筑螃蟹宝宝大军，建筑工挖掘宝藏，障碍物开辟道路帮助协防，祈祷师类似于向日葵提供货币，解锁仪式石，园艺师种植植物吸引其他物种，铲除入侵物种，物种死亡掉落食物，采集工搬运食物，战士来应对夜晚的入侵物种啃噬植物。 本作在较低难度下策略性比较有限，基本上不需要过多的去切换职业，从开头用到尾都可以，我打的是中间那档难度，所需要的操作也只是晚上切换一下建筑工的职业而已（因为AI比较蠢，大部分情况下晚上敌人入侵的时候建筑工都是去抗的，战士检测范围有些问题，没有检测到敌人导致看戏建筑工被殴打至死） 本作的roguelite属性则是：螃蟹宝宝每次升级时候的天赋三选一（一般通过升级的第一次确定后续职业）来围绕着进行进一步的构筑，仪式石也是有许多游戏内全局关卡buff以供选择，每一次关卡失败后都可以选择两次蟹蟹宝宝继承到下局游戏。 每个区域的地图有不同的植物以及物种，还有入侵生物的特性，以及螃蟹宝宝，仪式石，巢穴的数量不同 但比较可惜的是本作内容还是偏少，每个地图的流程也比较重复，也是期待后续的更新 [h2]改变世界[/h2] 本作部分关卡里设有守护石，玩家可以选择对应的公益渠道把自己为游戏贡献的收入献给世界环保组织，为海洋做出一份贡献，保护海洋就是保护世界 [h2]优化[/h2] 1.战士的ai应该优化，保卫家园的同时也要稍微保护一下建筑工，毕竟没了他就没法开拓道路继续向深海前进了（ 2.游戏加速：整体节奏上还是有很多不太需要操作的挂机时间，出一个自由切换游戏速度的快捷键会让节奏舒服很多 3.饮食系统还是稍慢了，特别是后期400多个食物的时候，可以出一个一键升级的功能 综上，本作目前还算不错，属于是未来可期那一档 [quote] 妙笔提手点墨花，妙语成章满纸纱。 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44852326/]猪式会社[/url]，用心绘测游戏。[/quote]

Ok, so this is a cute game, but it wasn't worth what I paid for it even on sale. I paid $14.39 with humble choice on sale. I have done 2 runs and while it's a cute fun little game, there wasn't much of an incentive for me to keep playing. Maybe if they gave you some perks at the end of a run, like letting you permanently keep 1 of the shrine effects you got during your run (with no duplicates). But even then, I think there needs to be some unlocks, like unlocking a different type of character or SOMETHING. There's just no replayability for me, and it's too short to feel like I got my money's worth on one run. There are a few other issues - sometimes it was literally impossible to fulfill the requirements of what a shrine wants. Like it wants you to have 3 of a fish, but to have that fish you need 18 of one thing and 9 of another thing and there are not enough slots for the plant/coral needed to support those populations. As a completionist, I find that pretty annoying. And i think it's odd that you can pick the same attributes for a crabling on level up more than once, I would think choosing one attribute would remove it from the random pool of attributes you can choose. Also, there should really be a button to auto pickup the worship points because scrolling back and forth to pick them up is a bit tedious. And why does the builder crab only attack things when it's right next to them and not auto like the hunter? Why do I have to click on the clams to smash them? Why doesn't the builder know to do that? I get that there would be "less to do" if you automate those things, but if your game is relying on really tedious busy actions to make the game seem like you are doing something, maybe that's an issue? I'm honestly kinda surprised this isn't an early access game because it really seems to lack features of a full game for this price. It IS very cute and a nice concept, I really like the premise, but it feels like they finished the first part of a game and said "send it, good enough".
Crabs good. Crab god good. Coral reefs good. Game good.
I'd recommend, but me personally, it got kinda boring.

It's such a charming experience for what it is. It's a relatively simple "town" building game where you manage a handful of crabs in order to restore the local ecosystems. Attract native wildlife and fight off invasive species at night. Might be a little repetitive to folks who expect more out of management games like this, but for what it is, it's perfectly fine and entertaining for a quick run or two. I could easily see this being the kind of educational game that's installed in school computer labs!

I like this game. It's a bit basic, but its worst features are how unpolished it is. Music towards the end of the game itself is actually corrupted. There's a patch of audio jank that completely ruins one of the few songs that you'll hear through this game's sparse soundtrack. That it's been this way for nearly a full year is inexcusable. Other problems include: -Cannot skip intro cinematic (or any of those). -Big problems with the scrolling, clearly meant for a tablet. -Lack of meaningful complexity later on (bit of a nit-pick). -Runs are short, but there isn't meaningful inter-run systems other than cosmetic unlocks. For a game this minimal, it's fine but considering your first run is ~4 hours long, overpriced by a pretty fair margin and you're really ripping yourself off if you don't go for multiple clears. Since it's structured like a Roguelike, you'd think the routes, hazards, etc are shuffled, but this is not the case. Especially after you've got like 10+ crabs in your possee, it's pretty easy to ignore a lot of the game's hazards. I like this game. It's fine! But some things like Cutscene Skipping, better UI to tell me how my crabs are doing, oh and fixing some selection hitboxes (crabgod help you if a crab is infront of one of the smaller plants/corals and you want to upgrade it). The music desperately needs a second pass to fix audio problems.
It's fun the first time you play it, but it really has no replay value sadly. The game does have potential if it gets updated though.

To my absolute core, I want to give this game a positive review, but I just can't. I do truly love it to some degree though. So from the absolute core, the game is trying to be far to many genres, and it does so kind of poorly. As well as another major issue, is the game just has corrupt sound files towards the end of a run, and finally, it just feels unfinished. I will not go so far as to call it slop or such, no it's beautiful, it's cute, it's adorable. I love the concept of this game, I love the art. You can tell a lot of care and love has been put into it, but somewhere, the suits or time caught up with them or something, I'm not sure. The core gameplay loop is kind of boring, you're basically playing an idle game, that has mini puzzles/resource management. It's not really complicated enough to really be called either, but it's not awful. There's not a lot of interaction you have with the crabs past assigning and reassigning roles. While this isn't a huge issue, it does lead to the core loop being, scrolling left and right repeatedly. Even if the game was just, harder, that'd solve nothing as you'd just lose, you can't really effect much. Mild/Major Spoilers Past this point As I said, the game feels unfinished, after the first couple levels, the levels feel very empty/samey, towards the end, the big build up coming to a climax, the stress of what happens in the final level, what happens when I tell the egg to hatch? Nothing, the game just ends. Everything you built up for, just stops. It's built with rogue like intentions, so everything is also just gone. You maybe unlocked a couple cosmetics, but no real story, no dramatic scenes. The goal you set out to complete is completed, and that's it. Wasn't hard, is that a problem? Eh, debatable, that's why there's difficulty settings, which this game does have. I fully intend to follow this game and see if anything more happens with it. I love what they're trying to do as a company, but to really keep a player base engaged, there needs to be a tad more to the content. I really dragged out my run to 5-6 hours taking my time, but you can absolutely blast through it far quicker. I will update my review if anything happens. The corrupted sound files towards the end of the game though is just kind of an unacceptable problem for a game that's been fully released for a year. I see there were some bug fixes back in august of last year and a couple of smaller updates for holiday stuff, but I don't have a lot of faith in what I'm seeing being fixed or addressed so at the end of the day, I don't actually recommend the game. It's fun for a couple of levels, but by the end of the first run, I just don't feel like I had a great experience. Luckily I got it from a humble bundle, so I don't feel ripped off, but I did basically buy the bundle only for this game and to try and few others (Which really ended up not being my flavour sadly, but I'm not going to give them reviews at all). All in all, get it for $10 or less, enjoy a couple of levels, but expect disappointment and maybe you'll enjoy it a bit more. My hopes weren't high past holy crap this game is cute, but I'm left wanting more. I don't regret the purchase, but I'm sure many would.

The entire game is clicking on farm plots and picking jobs for your crabs. I was told there would be "Rogue-lite elements" but that's just picking randomized buff / debuff combos that go better with certain jobs after every stage. Even worse, there are little / no worthwhile buffs for certain jobs like Hunter and Builder. You're far better off just taking generic buffs and using all of your crabs for 3 or so jobs and just swapping when there are mobs. The graphics are good and it's got a nice underwater vibe but this is on the shallow end. There's very little gameplay beyond switching jobs and initial farm tasks. Stages are just "get more food" which comes from fish killing each other. Fish start off blacked out, because isn't it more fun to have no information? The customization options are kind of lackluster beyond coloring. There's no notification or interaction with your crabs being killed / dying? The crab Hunter AI is awful, sometimes standing there with enemies a few inches away. Maybe a fun game for 12 year olds?
游戏类型：类肉鸽+经营模拟+类自走棋 优点：缝的创意很新颖，入手就玩了8小时。还能顺手保护一下海洋，后面还会发这笔钱的反馈，个人感觉比捐某基金会强。 缺点：内容和事件还是不够多，导致玩到后面就是无脑种花。 总结：如果30块对你来说不算多，那是值得一入的，玩游戏不就是去看各种不一样的世界么？最后再期待一下制作组对内容的更新好了。

While not necessarily bad, Crab God is unfortunately pretty middling. The game will frequently give you goals (Ritual Stones) that you can't complete with the types of corals/plants in the level. The interface for which fish need which requirements could be much improved, and they could've added an interface for which kinds of coral/plant could be grown where. Crabs don't prioritize tasks in a reasonable way (plenty of food laying around but only one scavenger crab actively collecting it, plenty of garden tasks all falling to one gardener crab, etc.) Levels just seem to drag on with little tension as you wait to get enough food to go to the next level. The upgrade crab screen at the end of each level for some reason demands more performance than the actual levels, so you have to sit through a fairly lengthy and laggy sequence for a bunch of upgrades that are, for the most part, pretty middling. It's not *bad* but I sure wish it were better, since I like the theme a lot!

Crab God, developed by Chaos Theory Games and published by Firesquid, offers a distinct and refreshing experience in the strategy and simulation genre by immersing players in an underwater world filled with vibrant life and delicate ecosystems. At its core, the game places you in the role of the Guardian of the Abyss, responsible for leading a colony of small crustacean-like creatures known as Crablings on a vital migration journey to ensure the birth of the next Crab God. This premise immediately sets the tone for a gameplay experience that balances careful management, environmental awareness, and a sense of nurturing responsibility. What sets Crab God apart from many other strategy games is the way it intertwines gameplay mechanics with a meaningful environmental message. The game goes beyond mere simulation by encouraging players to restore coral reefs, protect marine life, and fend off natural predators—all while carefully managing resources essential to the survival of your Crabling colony. The world feels alive and reactive; your decisions directly influence the health of the ecosystem, making every action carry weight. This intertwining of environmental stewardship and survival challenges encourages players to think thoughtfully about cause and effect within the game’s aquatic realm. The game’s art design plays a crucial role in creating this immersive atmosphere. With lush, colorful underwater scenes and charmingly animated Crablings, the visuals are both engaging and soothing, offering a peaceful yet compelling backdrop for the strategic gameplay. Every coral formation, swaying seaweed, and shimmering water effect enhances the feeling of being submerged in a living, breathing ecosystem. Accompanying this is an atmospheric soundtrack that further draws players into the serene yet tense mood of the underwater journey, striking a delicate balance between tranquility and the ever-present threats lurking in the depths. Gameplay in Crab God is accessible but rich with strategic depth. Players must constantly balance the needs of their Crabling colony, ensuring growth and safety while navigating environmental hazards and predators. Task management is key: deciding who gathers resources, who builds, and who protects the group requires both long-term planning and quick adaptation. The migration is not a simple linear path but a carefully orchestrated progression where timing and resource allocation are critical. This adds a satisfying layer of challenge that rewards attentive and thoughtful play. One of the most innovative and admirable aspects of Crab God is its integration of real-world ecological efforts through its partnership with dots.eco. In-game achievements and progression contribute to tangible environmental projects, such as planting trees, cleaning ocean plastic, and propagating coral reefs. This social impact angle elevates the game beyond entertainment, giving players a genuine sense of contributing to the health of the planet. It’s a rare and powerful example of how video games can bridge virtual actions with real-world benefits, making Crab God not just a game but a platform for awareness and positive change. While the game excels in many areas, there are moments when the pacing can feel slow, especially for players used to more action-packed strategy titles. The emphasis on thoughtful planning means progress can be methodical, and some may find the challenges less intense compared to more combat-focused strategy games. However, for those who appreciate a more meditative and meaningful approach, this slower pace enhances the experience rather than detracts from it. In summary, Crab God is a uniquely heartfelt and engaging strategy game that successfully marries thoughtful gameplay with an important environmental message. Its gorgeous underwater world, compelling colony management mechanics, and socially conscious design set it apart in a genre often dominated by combat and resource exploitation. For players looking for a game that invites reflection, strategic thinking, and a chance to make a real-world impact through play, Crab God offers a deeply satisfying and memorable journey beneath the waves. Rating: 8/10

Not being able to save during a level is awful. I have to afk the last 5-10 mins of each level to hit certain stone buffs or get more xp. When I clicked on migrate the game crashes and doesn't save the whole level that I just completed. I wanted to complete one full run to the end, but now I'd rather boot up a diff. game. Nice peaceful game, not for the tik tok generation.

The game has a good idea, a nice potential. The crablings are the kind of a lil guys i'd die for. The whole mechanic of creating an eco system is interesting in it's core. AND! It carries an educational thought about invasive species, the ones reprisented in the game are real life species that really do harm corals. And the devs are having an eco campaign with this game, which is incredible! But the realisation is awfully medoicre at best. First hour or so i was hooked, but from the start i've noticed that there's no real comprehensive tutorial. The game is quite simple, it wasn't too hard to figure things out, but i assume that it might push away some people. The balance in the game is mmm questionable. Walls are literally useless, while lvl 3 traps are already able to kill a lot of mobs. Some levels are full of places to build those said walls\traps, while some might literally have only one such place on one side of the level, which led me to my first death. And oh my god. Never before losing in a game made me so frustrated. Not because of the single fact i lost, but because of the PAINFULLY SLOW on death animation. Which i couldn't skip. I literally smashed every key on my keyboard in a hope it might save me. Nope. I'm not kiddind, i've opened my phone to read something while the animation was playing. I've started the second run just to see the end of that migration. Never before i've got so many bugs in a fully finished game. The game was crushing, the crablings were getting stuck in the animations etc. The gameplay kind of has rouge-like vibes. But it all ends on the vibes. There's no continuity between runs, if you're starting a new run it's a new run. It's not looping for an engaging playthrough. If you've finished the run one time - that's the most fun experience you'd have with this game. Every next run isn't bringing anything new and the sole reason why i wanted to play more is to unlock at least one fish companion for crabs. Oh and customisation of said crabs is lacking. A LOT. The options that are there feel like bread crumbs. The ones you can unlock require a lot of time. Mind you, i'm full on repetitive gameplay if it's fun. This game didn't bring me enough fun to open it ever again. Thank god i've got this game while it's on a sale, but even with a massive discount it feels like a waste of money.
Wholesome Game, All about protecting the ocean and has real life impact quests for saving the environment.

I liked the game and loved the real world impact idea (however small it might be). Was looking forward to completing the full run to see the ending. HOWEVER, a game where late missions tend to last an hour or more and autosaves only happen between said missions, does not have the luxury of crashing mid-level. That's a hard NO. Also, the UI is a rather lacking: when a wall gets swarmed by a ton of enemies, good luck clicking it to issue a repair order. Not gonna happen. On top of that, in my playthrough the walls became un-upgradeable at one point. In a nutshell, to many bugs for such a simple game.
It's fun, but I haven't been able to get the game to not crash for an entire thirty nights and it only saves between levels. Other than that it's an engaging little horizontal strategy game.

The graphics are great the gameplay loop is fun but gets old rather quick. More different enemies would help. The achievements are a chore. 30 nights is a lot and I don't know if the game can be in a world that long without crashing. A place showing all the perks, unlocks you have would make them feel like an achievement. More environments would help like different types of kelp forests. The ability to establish animals on maps that have the required plants would be good so you don't get 3 maps that don't have enough spots. An update with the above would make this game really fun. There's a whole world of potential inspiration in the ocean. tidal zones, orange kelp forest in California, purple reefs, crazy sharks, ground dwelling animals that blend in and they kill your crab if you don't have 2 attack at the same time. Being able to save during maps would also help. When the game crashes, you lose all the progress to an achievement like 30 nights.

B E C O M E C R A B. On a more serious note I enjoy the mechanic of different run levels and leveling up your crablings between them, so progression doesn't feel stale and there's always a fresh goal to work towards. So far I've only played Cozy mode, but the difficulty is just the right amount of micro management, and the challenges add another layer of fun. Love the customization, even if I wish the treasure dig sites ere a little more generous in giving gifts and not just favor and food. Being able to color code the crabs for their roles has been a lifesaver. 1000/10 for the real-world donations to environmental causes. I do keep getting small glitches in my runs such as walls getting stuck on Repair when they're at full health (including right after I've built them to lvl 1), or some treasure dig sites being un-clickable. Also wish some of the Green Mussels would stop landing on hard to access places like beneath traps. And crabs and other fish can often get in the way of me trying to click on a mussel or even a plant/coral to upgrade. But despite the small setbacks I've been enjoying the game immensely and I plan to sink many more hours into it. NOW GO AND BECOME CRAB!

I recently started playing this cute game and have really been enjoying it. However, I've encountered several bugs that I wanted to report. The most serious issue is that the game occasionally crashes with an error message, and there doesn't seem to be a proper way to submit a bug report from within the game. When this happens during a Habitat Migration, all progress from that migration is lost after restarting the game, forcing me to begin it again from the start. This has already happened to me around four times. I've also noticed a few smaller issues: Sometimes, when upgrading walls, a small crab gets stuck and the upgrade never finishes unless I manually cancel it and start the upgrade again. Walls occasionally become stuck in the "Repair" state even when they're already at full health, including immediately after building them to level 1. Some treasure dig sites cannot be clicked. Green mussels sometimes land in difficult-to-reach places, such as underneath traps. Crabs and other sea creatures often block clicks when I'm trying to collect mussels or upgrade plants and corals. Despite these bugs and minor glitches, I've been enjoying the game immensely and plan to spend many more hours playing it. I hope these issues can be fixed in a future update!
